1.15.2.en: Silver signifies the treasures of the rich, and wine signifies love and affection; the formalist in his faith resorts to the wisdom of the world as a deceptive treasure that has the appearance of precious silver while it is dross; and he appears full of love and affection while his heart carries water (without warmth).

1.15.3.en: St. Irenaeus sees that the elders were accustomed to mixing the wine of God's simple commandments with the water of human tradition, which is contrary to the word of truth. And St. Gregory of Nazianzus says: [We are not like the many who are able to corrupt the word of truth and to mix with water the wine that maketh glad the heart of man (Ps 104:15), that is, to mix our teaching with what is trite and cheap and base and worn out and tasteless.]

1.16.0.en: D. "Thy princes are rebellious, and companions of thieves" [23], that is, they eat with the thieves and keep their clothes during the theft. It was fitting for the leaders to manage the affairs of the people and shepherd them, but they turned shepherding into authority and toil; they may not steal, but they leave the enemy of good with his soldiers to rob the people and seize their hearts, while they are indifferent because of their love of authority. They love bribes and material or moral gifts, and do not care for the orphans and widows, because temporal glory occupied them from thinking of them. They turned Jerusalem, "the Church of Christ," into a house of injustice, cruelty and violence.

1.16.1.en: Instead of the leaders being a living example for the people in submission to the word of God and in practicing the godly life, they became a stumbling block to them. St. Irenaeus says: [From the ages of the Law the scribes and Pharisees began to despise God and not to accept His word, that is, they did not believe in Christ.]

1.17.s.en: 9. The Judge comes forward as a Savior:

1.17.0.en: 24 Therefore saith the Lord, the LORD of hosts, the mighty One of Israel, Ah, I will ease me of mine adversaries, and avenge me of mine enemies: 25 And I will turn my hand upon thee, and purely purge away thy dross, and take away all thy tin: 26 And I will restore thy judges as at the first, and thy counsellors as at the beginning: afterward thou shalt be called, The city of righteousness, the faithful city. 27 Zion shall be redeemed with judgment, and her converts with righteousness. 28 And the destruction of the transgressors and of the sinners shall be together, and they that forsake the LORD shall be consumed. 29 For they shall be ashamed of the oaks which ye have desired, and ye shall be confounded for the gardens that ye have chosen. 30 For ye shall be as an oak whose leaf fadeth, and as a garden that hath no water. 31 And the strong shall be as tow, and the maker of it as a spark, and they shall both burn together, and none shall quench them.

1.17.1.en: Before this hideous picture God does not stand with folded hands, but "the LORD of hosts, the mighty One of Israel" [24] rises as the Commander of the heavenly armies, whose hand is strong with might for the salvation of His people from what has befallen them.

1.17.3.en: A. He called God by three titles [the Lord (Yahweh), the LORD of hosts, the mighty One of Israel]. Some scholars see in this a hidden reference to the Holy Trinity. The Father is the incomprehensible and invisible (Yahweh = I Am), the Word who became incarnate to lead the battle against the enemy of good, granting His soldiers every spiritual victory, and the mighty Holy Spirit who works in the believers to form them in the image of Christ, so that they find for themselves a portion in the bosom of the Father.

1.18.0.en: And Jerusalem bore 3 titles: the city of righteousness, the faithful city, Zion redeemed by justice [26-27].

1.19.0.en: The wicked were also called by three titles: the transgressors, the sinners, those who forsake the LORD [28].

1.19.1.en: B. God counts the one who destroys His people a heavy burden (Isa 3:14-15), so He does not cease to resist evil until He rests and His people rest with Him: "I will ease me of mine adversaries, and avenge me of mine enemies" [24].

1.19.2.en: The bowels of the Lord remain yearning over His people until evil is shattered!

1.19.3.en: C. "He purges Jerusalem of the dross as with borax (perhaps he means the potash of metals)"; for He recreates human nature to restore to the Church her original beauty, as by the purifying fire of the Holy Spirit.

1.19.4.en: He also purifies us by discipline, though it appear harsh as fire:

1.19.5.en: * Blessed is the man who is disciplined in this life, for the Lord does not punish twice for one thing (Nah 1:9) LXX.

1.19.6.en: * A father does not discipline his son if he does not love him, and a teacher does not set right his pupil unless he sees in him signs of obtaining the promise. When a physician withdraws his care from a patient, it is counted a sign that he despairs of his recovery.

1.19.7.en: St. Jerome * God rebukes in order to correct, and corrects in order to keep us for Himself.

1.19.8.en: St. Cyprian D. "And I will restore thy judges as at the first" [26]. For He restores man to his dignity and reason as at the beginning of his creation, so that he is like a wise judge.

1.19.9.en: E. He restores to Jerusalem, or to the human soul, her title: "the city of righteousness, the faithful city" [26]. For the Church, the new Jerusalem, the city of God, the pillar and ground of the truth, the faithful bride of her Bridegroom, is filled with the redeemed penitents who bear the righteousness of Christ in them; but those who forsake the Lord or reject Him have no place in the true Church and no portion in the heavenly Church. These are filled with shame because they desired the world, the terebinth trees, and counted it their garden, and the world was lost and their hopes were lost.

1.19.10.en: The world is likened here to the terebinth, because the Jews were accustomed to setting up the worship of Baal and Ashtoreth under the terebinth tree.

1.20.0.en: Those who forsake the Lord are likened to the terebinth whose leaf has withered, and to the garden that has no water [29]. Why? God created man as a garden in which the Lord finds his fruit sweet within. All the energies, capacities, feelings and instincts that man bears are divine gifts, like trees planted in a garden watered by the water of the Holy Spirit, so that they bear countless blessings. But if the Spirit is withheld from it, it dries up and is burned with fire, and turns into tow (the refuse of flax) [31], that is, what remains of flax after it is combed, to be used as fuel for fire.

2.0.0.en: "The things that Isaiah the son of Amoz saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem:" [1].

2.0.1.en: Isaiah's heart was occupied with the people of God (Judah) and with the holy city (Jerusalem); he was filled with sorrow at the state to which things had come, seeing a people struck by corruption and a city whose spiritual temple was being torn down, so that his bowels moaned over it.

2.0.2.en: Before this pure love God gave him insight and presented him with visions and prophecies to comfort him, and to comfort every soul wounded for the sake of mankind; God presented to him His life-giving Word.

2.0.3.en: * The (Word) came to (Hosea, Isaiah and Jeremiah) and enlightened the prophets with the light of knowledge, and made them see things which they did not understand at that time.

2.1.s.en: 2. The mountain of the LORD's house:

2.1.0.en: 2 And it shall come to pass in the last days, that the mountain of the LORD'S house shall be established in the top of the mountains, and shall be exalted above the hills; and all nations shall flow unto it. 3 And many people shall go and say, Come ye, and let us go up to the mountain of the LORD, to the house of the God of Jacob; and he will teach us of his ways, and we will walk in his paths: for out of Zion shall go forth the law, and the word of the LORD from Jerusalem. 4 And he shall judge among the nations, and shall do justice for many peoples: and they shall beat their swords into plowshares, and their spears into pruninghooks: nation shall not lift up sword against nation, neither shall they learn war any more. 5 O house of Jacob, come ye, and let us walk in the light of the LORD.

2.1.1.en: What did God offer to Isaiah, wounded in soul? He carried him in the Spirit to the fullness of time to see the new Judah, the Lord Christ, and the new Jerusalem, where the temple of the Lord is built and the Kingdom of God is established in the heart... He sees the holy congregation coming from all the nations and peoples to worship the Lord in spirit and in truth in Jesus Christ, the Savior of the world. Therefore he said: "And it shall come to pass in the last days, that the mountain of the LORD'S house shall be established in the top of the mountains, and shall be exalted above the hills; and all nations shall flow unto it" [2].

2.1.2.en: Some see that this prophecy was taken by Isaiah from the prophet Micah (Mic 4:1-5), or perhaps both took it from an earlier source. But what prevents the Holy Spirit from granting the same gift, prophecy, to the two prophets and to others, when He finds in them a sincere heart, burning for the salvation and building up of man, and so presents it to Isaiah in the days of Ahaz and to Micah in the days of Hezekiah, to confirm that what the inspiration utters will not fall?

2.1.3.en: The Lord drew Isaiah's heart to the fullness of time to see the Lord Christ, on whom He Himself establishes His Church, being the Rock of ages, the mountain that the prophet Daniel saw, cut out without hands, which filled the earth (Dan 2:34, 45), the true Rock from which the waters of the Spirit flow to His people (1 Cor 10:4), and upon which the serpent cannot crawl to approach His people.

2.1.4.en: St. Augustine says: [The mountain, as the prophetic testimony teaches us, is the Lord Himself.]

2.1.5.en: * There are also mountains that are not known because they stand in certain places on the earth... But this mountain is otherwise, for it filled the whole face of the earth; of it it was said, "shall be established in the top of the mountains," it is a mountain standing above the summits of all mountains, "and all nations shall flow unto it."

2.1.6.en: Who is unable to perceive what this mountain is?!

2.1.7.en: Who is this who breaks his head by resisting this mountain?!

2.1.8.en: Who is ignorant of the city that stands upon the mountain?!

2.1.9.en: Do not wonder if this city is unknown to those who hate the brethren, for they walk in darkness and know not whither they go, because darkness has blinded their eyes. They do not see the mountain.

2.1.10.en: I want you not to wonder, for they are without eyes; how? Because darkness has blinded them. Prove it? Because they hate the brethren!

2.1.11.en: St. Augustine The Lord founded His Church when He was lifted up onto the mountain of temptation (Mt 4:8) to give her the spirit of overcoming and victory over the powers of darkness; He went to the mountain Himself, and as St. Jerome says: [He did not go up as one who is compelled or as a captive, but was led with longing for the battle], and St. John Chrysostom also says: [Satan went to man (Adam) to tempt him, but since Satan cannot attack Christ, Christ went to him.]

2.1.12.en: He also founded His Church on the mountain of teaching (Mt 5:1), where He gave His people His commandment, the secret of life. And also on Mount Tabor, where He declared His glory and entered with His Church into the very heavens (Lk 9:41), and finally on Mount Golgotha, where she delighted in her Bridegroom, the sacrificed one, the Savior of mankind by His precious blood. On this mountain the Lord stretched out His hands on the Cross to draw all men unto Him (Jn 12:32); therefore the prophet continues, saying: "and all nations shall flow unto it. And many people shall go and say, Come ye, and let us go up to the mountain of the LORD, to the house of the God of Jacob; and he will teach us of his ways, and we will walk in his paths: for out of Zion shall go forth the law, and the word of the LORD from Jerusalem" [2-3].

2.1.13.en: It is known that the Law was given from Mount Sinai to the Jewish people; therefore he speaks of a new law going forth from Jerusalem, addressed to the whole world.

2.1.14.en: * This Law is not the property of one nation but of all the nations, for the law of the Lord and His word do not remain in Zion and Jerusalem but spread through the whole world. Therefore the Intercessor Himself says to His fearful disciples: "These are the words which I spake unto you, while I was yet with you, that all things must be fulfilled, which were written in the law of Moses, and in the prophets, and in the psalms, concerning me..." (Lk 24:44-47). This is the universal way of the salvation of the soul which was announced before by the angels and the holy prophets...

2.1.15.en: * There (in Jerusalem) He told the disciples: "Go ye therefore, and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit" (Mt 28:19).

2.1.16.en: * It was necessary that (the Holy Spirit) be given after the resurrection of Christ in the same city in which the new Law, that is, the New Testament, begins; for the first Law, which is called the Old Testament, was given on Mount Sinai through Moses, but this one was given through Christ, as was foretold of it: "out of Zion shall go forth the law, and the word of the LORD from Jerusalem."

2.1.17.en: St. Augustine It is observed that this Church, founded on Mount Golgotha and going forth from Jerusalem, bears the power of the Holy Spirit, as follows:

2.1.18.en: A. A steadfast Church, standing on the established mountain of the LORD's house [2]; the Apostle Paul calls it "mount Sion," saying: "But ye are come unto mount Sion, and unto the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, and to an innumerable company of angels, to the general assembly and church of the firstborn, which are written in heaven" (Heb 12:22-23). The secret of her strength and steadfastness is the Lord Himself, who sanctifies her to Himself and raises her to His heavens so that she bears His traits.

2.1.19.en: B. High on the top of the mountains [2]; she has become the light of the world, proclaiming the truth openly without fear (Acts 16:26). Her members stand in the body on the earth, but their hearts and thoughts are lifted up as above the high mountains, soaring in the air of heaven. As Origen says: [It is enough that you not remain on the earth, nor dwell in the valleys, nor linger in buried places.]

2.1.20.en: C. Attractive to the nations and peoples [2-3]: her doors are open to all, bearing a motherhood of love toward all mankind, drawn from the love of her Bridegroom, who gathers all men.

2.2.0.en: D. Her continual work is to lift mankind up [3]. In love she comes down to them without losing her holiness or her heavenly nature, in order to raise all, by the Spirit of the holy God, to the Jerusalem above, that they may practice the new heavenly life in Christ Jesus.

2.2.1.en: E. Her mission is to declare the way of the Lord [3]; she carries His word to every soul and presents His commandment for every believer to live by, so that he enjoys the law of liberty (Gal 4:26).

2.2.2.en: F. She proclaims the righteous judgments of Christ, where the believers from all the nations submit to His Kingdom and sovereignty, a spiritual sovereignty unique in its kind.

2.3.0.en: G. She grants peace among the souls sanctified to Him, for they see no human enemies on the whole face of creation. Therefore he says: "and they shall beat their swords into plowshares, and their spears into pruninghooks: nation shall not lift up sword against nation, neither shall they learn war any more" [4]. The Christian's heart is filled with peace even toward his opponents, so that his inner energies are turned from conflict to constructive work, from instruments of war to instruments of production for prosperity.

2.3.1.en: The word of God turns earth into heaven, so heavenly peace dwells in the life of men, and the kingdom of peace, or the joyful Kingdom of God, is established within them, which neither the enmity of men nor the harshness of events can shake.

2.3.2.en: * Men went out from Jerusalem into the world, twelve in number; they were unlettered, with no ability to speak, but by the power of God they declared to every race of men that they were sent by Christ to teach all the wisdom of God. And we who formerly fought one another have not only refrained from war against our enemies but have also come to the point that we do not lie or deceive those who examine us (for trial), and we die willingly, confessing Christ.

2.4.0.en: The Martyr Justin H. Enjoying Christ, "the light of the LORD," as Isaiah the prophet heard: "O house of Jacob, come ye, and let us walk in the light of the LORD" [5]. The Lord Christ, who dwells in His Church, is the brightness of the Father's glory and the express image of His person, upholding all things by the word of His power (Heb 1:3); He is the Sun of righteousness with healing in its wings (Mal 4:2). He shines upon His Church, and she herself becomes a light to the world, giving light to those who sit in the darkness of sin, presenting her Christ to everyone.

2.4.1.en: This call addressed to the house of Jacob to walk in the light of the LORD is a call to lift the veil of the letter from the Law, so that the house of Jacob may discover the "Messiah" hidden behind the words, enjoying the word of God not as literal commandments but as fellowship with Christ, the true Light.

2.4.2.en: Who are the house of Jacob? The Martyr Justin answers: [It is fitting for us here to observe that there are two seeds of Judah, there are two, as there are two houses of Jacob; one born of flesh and blood and the other of faith and the Spirit.]

2.5.s.en: 3. The reason for God's rejection of His people:

2.5.0.en: 6 For thou hast rejected thy people the house of Jacob, because they be replenished from the east, and are diviners like the Philistines, and they clasp hands with the children of strangers. 7 Their land also is full of silver and gold, neither is there any end of their treasures; their land is also full of horses, neither is there any end of their chariots: 8 Their land also is full of idols; they worship the work of their own hands, that which their own fingers have made: 9 And the mean man boweth down, and the great man humbleth himself: therefore forgive them not.

2.5.1.en: The prophet compares the conduct of his contemporary people with the conduct of the nations in the future, when they accept faith in the saving God and enter the Kingdom of peace and enjoy transcendent blessings by dwelling on the mountain of the LORD's house.

2.5.2.en: The house of Jacob in practice rejected God, in spite of its intense concern for the literalism of worship; therefore God rejected it, and this was a type of the Jews' rejection of the person of the Lord Christ under the cover of their defense of the truth and their zeal for the Law of Moses.

2.5.3.en: God presented four reasons for rejecting the people, namely: imitating strangers, their love of the wealth of the world, their reliance on their military capabilities, and their acceptance of idol worship.

2.5.4.en: A. Imitating strangers: "they be replenished from the east" [6].

2.5.5.en: God had set them apart for Himself to be filled with His Spirit, to bear His heavenly wisdom, and to be witnesses of the truth and a holy leaven for the world; but they opened their doors to strangers, especially the sons of the east, learning from them sorcery, idol worship and abominations, instead of bearing witness before them to God's work in them. For the sake of material gain and indulgence in abominations they encouraged the pagans to settle in their midst, and mixed with them (Hos 7:8), and betrayed the divine covenant.

2.5.6.en: He also says: "and are diviners like the Philistines" [6]. Instead of returning to God in all their affairs, they imitated the Philistines of that time, resorting to augury and soothsaying, contrary to the divine commandment (Lev 19:26).

2.5.7.en: B. Their preoccupation with the wealth of the world and material things: "Their land also is full of silver and gold, neither is there any end of their treasures." Their hearts were filled with the love of money, so they counted it able to satisfy them, and it took the place of God in their thought and feelings.

2.6.0.en: C. Their reliance on their military capabilities: "their land is also full of horses, neither is there any end of their chariots" [7]. They relied on horses and chariots instead of faith and returning to God.

2.7.0.en: D. Their acceptance of idol worship [8].

2.8.0.en: These are the reasons for which God rejected His people, and the fruit of that is continual decline instead of growth and ascent [9]. A collapse in every aspect of life instead of complete sanctification by the Lord who ascended into the heavens.

2.9.s.en: 4. The futility of the human arm:

2.9.0.en: 10 Enter into the rock, and hide thee in the dust, for fear of the LORD, and for the glory of his majesty. 11 The lofty looks of man shall be humbled, and the haughtiness of men shall be bowed down, and the LORD alone shall be exalted in that day. 12 For the day of the LORD of hosts shall be upon every one that is proud and lofty, and upon every one that is lifted up; and he shall be brought low: 13 And upon all the cedars of Lebanon, that are high and lifted up, and upon all the oaks of Bashan, 14 And upon all the high mountains, and upon all the hills that are lifted up, 15 And upon every high tower, and upon every fenced wall, 16 And upon all the ships of Tarshish, and upon all the pleasant banners. 17 And the loftiness of man shall be bowed down, and the haughtiness of men shall be made low: and the LORD alone shall be exalted in that day. 18 And the idols he shall utterly abolish. 19 And they shall go into the holes of the rocks, and into the caves of the earth, for fear of the LORD, and for the glory of his majesty, when he ariseth to shake terribly the earth. 20 In that day a man shall cast his idols of silver, and his idols of gold, which they made each one for himself to worship, to the rats and to the bats; 21 To go into the clefts of the rocks, and into the tops of the ragged rocks, for fear of the LORD, and for the glory of his majesty, when he ariseth to shake terribly the earth. 22 Cease ye from man, whose breath is in his nostrils: for wherein is he to be accounted of?

2.9.1.en: If God has rejected His people, it is because His people insist on rejecting God by every means, but God remains in His love compassionate toward them and toward all mankind, declaring His salvation to man.

2.9.2.en: When man grows exceedingly great in his own eyes and the ego swells, the Lord reveals His glory, and man shrinks and seeks salvation. He enters as into a rock and hides in the dust before the fear of the LORD and the glory of His majesty [10]. When God appeared to Abraham, the father of fathers realized that he was dust and ashes, and when Moses saw the glory of the Lord he was afraid and trembled, and so the soul of Job clung to the dust. Nothing shatters man's pride like his meeting with God. The pride is shattered but his soul is not shattered; rather, it is healed and filled with hope in the Lord.

2.9.3.en: What is the rock in which we hide before the divine majesty but the Lord Christ, for in Him we find a refuge for ourselves before divine justice. Therefore, when the prophet Moses desired to see the divine glory, it was said to him: "Thou canst not see my face: for there shall no man see me, and live... Behold, there is a place by me, and thou shalt stand upon a rock (Christ our Rock): and it shall come to pass, while my glory passeth by, that I will put thee in a clift of the rock (union with Christ), and will cover thee with my hand while I pass by" (Ex 33:20-21).

2.9.4.en: As long as we lean on our Christ, the true Rock, and abide in Him and are found as in a cleft within Him, we see the brightness of the divine glory; but if we trust in ourselves or in the human arm, we perish and are deprived of beholding God.

2.9.5.en: The prophet likens man's arrogance to the following:

2.10.0.en: A. "All the cedars of Lebanon, that are high and lifted up, and all the oaks of Bashan" [13] signify reliance on the wealth of nature's resources, and they also signify arrogant kings and leaders such as Rabshakeh.

2.11.0.en: B. "The high mountains and the hills that are lifted up" [14] signify hardness and rigidity, and perhaps they also mean the great kingdoms and the small kingdoms whose rule is pride together with violence.

2.12.0.en: C. "Every high tower and every fenced wall" [15] signify reliance on works of self-righteousness, for man is able to rise up high and fortify himself against every enemy; perhaps they signify the fortified cities.

2.13.0.en: D. "The ships of Tarshish, the ornaments and the pleasant banners" [16] signify absorption in trade and money, with luxury and wealth at the expense of care for the soul.

2.13.1.en: All these comparisons revolve around man's self-reliance and reliance on the capabilities of nature and its resources, with his continual progress, thinking that he is able by himself to create an atmosphere of satiety, joy and peace, with security and stability in the world, ignoring the divine arm. For this reason he needs the Lord to appear to him, to reveal to him the passing away of all these things, especially in the great day of the Lord.

2.14.0.en: Pride has been linked to idol worship; therefore the prophet affirms that when man discovers the helplessness of the idols, he throws them to the rats and the bats [20], treating them with contempt, instead of taking them with him on his journeys to support him. Instead of honoring them in places of worship he casts them into dark abandoned places where mice and bats play with them.

2.15.0.en: Finally man realizes the error of relying on the human arm, and the prophet says: "Cease ye from man, whose breath is in his nostrils: for wherein is he to be accounted of?!" [22]. Let every man be silent, however great his greatness, power or wealth, for the breath of his life goes forth and he is no longer in the world. His spirit goes forth and he returns to the dust (Ps 104:29).
